title: Egg Lottery
text: “So he’s gone. What should we do now? I guess, specifically, we just need to keep peddling until the time comes, but how should we handle this windfall?”
We’ll discuss our next steps in a back alley. That said, it’d probably be better to have a deeper conversation about it in the carriage.
“We’re going to look for Filo-tan.”
“Not again… Well, since that’s Motoyasu-kun’s goal, I won’t complain. So… should we look for this girl named Filo?”
“That’s right. Given the timing, I think my future Father used the money he received this time to acquire Filo-tan.”
“Hmm… The question is where and how he got her, right?”
“Exactly. Last time, he bought up the entire stock from the monster merchant, but she wasn’t there.”
“He bought them all up… Motoyasu-kun really goes all out, doesn’t he? But I think this is going to be a tough problem. It’d be great if there were any distinctive features we could use as a clue…”
“In her Filolial form, her color scheme is almost identical to Sakura-chan’s. In her Queen form, it’s the complete opposite.”
“She looks like Sakura?”
I nod at Sakura-chan’s words. After all, Filo-tan’s base color is white with hints of cherry blossom pink.
“Come to think of it, you were sketching her while we were riding in the carriage, weren’t you?”
“Her angel form looks completely different. She has the same build as Yuki-chan and the others, with blonde hair and blue eyes—she looks absolutely adorable.”

“Sakura-chan’s eyes are blue, but… her hair is cherry blossom pink, after all. Still, the fact that her color scheme changes so drastically when she takes on her angel form is definitely a unique trait. I remember the sketch Motoyasu-kun drew.”
Father’s point is well taken. I believe it’s quite rare—except for Filo-tan—for the color scheme to differ this much between her Filolial form and her angelic form.

However, if Filo-tan were to end up belonging to someone else, the only way to verify her identity would be when she’s in her Filolial form. Her angelic form and Queen form cannot be identified unless the Hero possesses her. Since the criteria for judgment are the color scheme and eye color of her Filolial form… and her scent, it’s certainly a difficult task.

“Apparently, my future self was a mess because he had no one to help him… so I think he’d only buy from someone he could rely on and trust. I’m pretty sure he bought her from that slave trader. Unless he made some impulse buy somewhere, that is.”
“Did my brother buy her from that slave trader?”
“I have a hunch. That person is, well… let’s say honest when it comes to money—he gives a hand with the idea of investing in the future, you know?”

That’s exactly what I’d expect. I know, too, that it was that monster merchant who supported my Father behind the scenes. I believe I heard it was also the monster merchant who arranged for my Big Sister to come here, and that he went out of his way to gather slaves from her hometown to help rebuild the village.

Also, I believe I heard that in the future, Big Sister had her slave mark removed. But wasn’t she still a slave the next time we met? I haven’t confirmed the details, but I seem to recall hearing something like that from Big Sister herself.
If that’s the case, we can’t completely rule out the possibility that she went to the monster merchant to have the slave mark reapplied. However, I don’t know what happened after that.
“I don’t really want to go, but since it’s Motoyasu-kun’s request, maybe I’ll drop by?”
“Thank you so much, Father!”
I’d go to any lengths to find Filo-tan. So, we headed straight for the Monster Merchant’s tent.

Yuki-chan and Kou hesitated to enter the Monster Merchant’s tent. It’s true there’s a somewhat gloomy atmosphere there—Filolial-sama generally doesn’t like to go near it. The Lazy Pig said he’d rather not deal with the hassle and would wait outside with Yuki-chan and the others.
“Well, well, my heroes. What brings you here today?”
As we entered the Monster Merchant’s tent, the merchant greeted us. He was rubbing his hands together. Not to be outdone, I rubbed my hands together for my Father too.
“Motoyasu-kun, why are you trying to one-up him?”
“Just on a whim.”
Now, I really want him to introduce me to Filo-tan. With that in mind, I keep rubbing my hands together in front of my Father.
“Hey, that guy with the spear—is he really…”
“Keel, it’d be too cruel to let you finish that…”
“Got it, bro.”
Keel is looking at me with a pitying gaze for some reason, but I’m not bothered by it at all. Sakura-chan is gazing blankly around inside the tent.
“Oh?”
The Monster Merchant stares at Keel and tilts his head.
“So you possess the ability to transform into a Beastman? Right. Well then, I suppose I should bump up the purchase price.”
“Huh!? Are you selling me, bro!?”
“I’m not selling you! Why did this suddenly turn into a conversation about selling Keel-kun—!?”
My Father, who’s been forced into “business mode,” is careful not to use the honorific “-kun” when addressing Keel.
“As expected of the Shield Hero—you’ve selected a slave who’s grown to be quite sturdy. I’m completely outmatched by your discerning eye, Hero. Yes.”
It seems the Monster Merchant has observed Keel’s growth and analyzed it.
“That’s right. With a coat this glossy—even though his build is a bit flimsy—I think he’d fetch a good price as a pet. Yes.”
The monster merchant is fiddling with some sort of device. From the looks of it, is that an abacus?

“Based on a quick appraisal, how about five gold coins? The price could go up if he’s still in his Demi-Human form. With that glossy coat—and if his appearance develops well—twelve gold coins would be a safe bet. Yes.”
“Big bro!”

Keel is looking at him with eyes like Filolial-sama when she was about to be sold. Oh?　Yuki-chan and Kou, who’ve gotten bored outside the tent, have started singing. It somehow reminds me of that song about being taken to the market on a sunny afternoon.
“Those two… even if it’s a coincidence, I wish they’d read the room…”
My father, clicking his tongue as he glares outside, soothes Keel—who’s clinging to him—while answering.
“S-sorry, but I have no intention of selling this guy now that he’s grown to be useful.”
“Is that so…? That’s a great pity. However…”
The monster merchant stares intently at Keel.
“I thought you’d be more like us, but you’ve fallen short of my expectations.”
Keel is clinging to my Father, looking worried. Is he really that scary?
“I’ll tell him that a true slave master keeps them neither alive nor dead, while still improving their quality…”
His father replies in full business mode. Should I apply this philosophy to myself?

Filolial-sama is a being worthy of equal love. Neither let them live nor let them die… and improve their quality? Yes… just like my own children—whether they’re quick or slow, strong or weak, smart or silly—I raise them all with equal care.
There’s absolutely no room for “quality” to come into play here. Every child has their own individuality. There’s no need for conflict or competition. I simply cannot understand it.

“The slaves you know are probably just disposable, aren’t they? That’s not productive at all. Don’t you think that making slaves swear allegiance without a slave mark and sending them to their deaths is what a true slave master does?”
However, the monster merchant seemed satisfied with Father’s reply.
“……Heh heh heh. Is that so? I’m getting a thrill out of this.”
“B-Brother?”

Keel’s face turned pale at Father’s words. Given what happened the day before… Father turned to Keel, raised his index finger as if to signal “secret,” and directed his gaze toward the monster merchant. Keel seemed to understand and gave a slight nod.
“So, what brings you to us this time? Yes?”
“Ah, well… this time…”
Father looked around inside the tent.
“I’m thinking of raising some new monsters. After all, we could use some extra combat power.”
“Is that so! Then what kind of monsters are you looking for? Since we’re on the subject, how about a flying dragon? It’s a bit pricey, but would you like to take a look? Yes?”
The monster merchant pressed Father with rapid-fire questions. Father furrowed his brow but held his ground, meeting the merchant’s gaze with equal intensity.
“A dragon wouldn’t be bad… but I’d prefer something like a Filolial. Was the specific breed called the Aria species?”
“You seem to be on the fence. In that case, how about trying the Monster Egg Lottery? Yes.”
“Monster Egg Lottery…?”
The monster merchant points to a wooden crate filled with eggs in the corner of the tent. It costs 100 silver coins to try, and it seems you have no idea what’s inside.
“Ah, so there are no winners in there, is that it? You’re running a pretty shady business.”
“What! Do you, the Hero, really think we’re running such a dishonest business!?”
“Is that not the case?”
“I take great pride in my business. While I do enjoy deceiving customers with lies, I detest misrepresenting the items I sell.”
“You like to deceive, but you hate misrepresentation… So, what’s the prize?”
“To put it simply for you, Hero, it’s a dragon mount.”
“Um… I think it’s a dragon that serves as a mount, like Filolial-sama, right?”
“This time, it’s a flying type… a flying dragon. Yes. Since it’s popular… our noble customers are taking on the challenge. Yes.”
My father is grumbling. Acting uninterested here would lower my business reputation. I suppose I’ll just watch in silence, too.
“If… Motoyasu-kun weren’t here and there were only one slave…”
My father is muttering to himself. I can tell he’s thinking things through.
